_comment: Non-US reference prices. Every figure is a published national average with its source and date — nothing here is invented. These are DEFAULT starting values only; every page lets the user override them.

dcFastCharging.basis: Representative US national average for non-member DC fast charging, compiled from published 2026 network pricing (Tesla Supercharger ~$0.42/kWh, EVgo ~$0.45/kWh, Electrify America ~$0.48/kWh mid-points).
dcFastCharging.caveat: Per-kWh pricing is not universal: several states require per-minute pricing, and most networks add idle or session fees. Treat as an estimate, not a quote.
dcFastCharging.confidence: estimate — PRD marks the DCFC source list as [待确认]; no single official dataset exists.

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.source: Ofgem default tariff price cap, July–September 2026
countries.note: Unit rate on a standard variable tariff. A separate daily standing charge (roughly 57p/day) applies and is not included.

countries.name: Germany
countries.source: Verivox analysis of household electricity prices, Q2 2026 (highest in the G20)
countries.note: Taxes, levies and grid fees make up more than 60% of the German household price.

countries.name: Canada
countries.source: Natural Resources Canada (NRCan) national residential average
countries.note: Provincial rates vary widely — Quebec and hydro-rich provinces sit well below the national average.

countries.name: Australia
countries.note: Excludes daily supply charges, which differ materially between states.

countries.name: India
countries.note: State tariffs and slab-based pricing mean the effective rate rises steeply with monthly consumption.
